title: Anger (Matthew 5:21–26)
hookLine: before you bring your gift, go and be reconciled

lines: A FURIOUS SPEECH IN THE SHOWER.
cards: Thou shalt not kill. It sounds like a commandment almost anyone could keep. But then there's the name muttered under the breath at a brother or sister.
The furious speech rehearsed in the shower, to someone who isn't there. Walking into church, a family dinner or a meeting while someone in the room is still upset, and just carrying on.
Jesus has said: go deeper, to the heart. Now he shows what that means, starting with one of the Ten Commandments.

teach.h: YE HAVE HEARD, BUT I SAY.
teach.b: Ye have heard, he says, that it was said, thou shalt not kill. But I say unto you: whoever is angry with his brother is in danger of judgment.
And whoever calls him raca, an insult usually explained as Aramaic for empty-head, is in danger too. It's the first of several times in this chapter Jesus says ye have heard, but I say unto you.
He isn't canceling the commandment. He's following it back to its root. Murder starts somewhere: in contempt, in the name you call someone, in the grudge you feed.

teach.h: LEAVE THY GIFT BEFORE THE ALTAR.
teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift."
Picture it. You've traveled to the temple with a gift to offer.
You're at the altar, and you remember that someone has something against you. Not that you're angry with them: they're angry with you. Leave the gift right there, Jesus says.
Go. Make it right. Then come back.

teach.h: FIRST BE RECONCILED TO THY BROTHER.
teach.b: The Greek word is diallasso: to be reconciled, to make things up with someone. Your neighbor isn't separate from your worship. Christians say God cares about both, and here the neighbor comes first.

how: In churches that share the peace during the service, it often comes before the gifts are brought to the altar or before communion, a custom some link to this passage, and some Christians make a point of mending quarrels before receiving communion or before Easter.

o: a feeling Jesus calls always harmless
a sin only if you act on it with your hands
the root Jesus traces murder back to

games.q: what's inside the teaching — tap the pairs.

s: Jesus cancels the commandment thou shalt not kill
he follows it back to its root in anger and contempt.
in the story, it's the other person who has something against you
thy brother hath ought against thee.
Jesus says to offer the gift first and make peace afterward
first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.

games.q: you've traveled to the temple with your offering. you're at the altar, and you remember someone has something against you. what do you do?
o: offer the gift, then deal with it later.
leave the gift, go and be reconciled, then come back.
pray for them at the altar.
games.why: "Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother." the neighbor comes first.

practice: Let one face come to mind: someone you're angry with, or, like the story's twist, someone who has something against you, and notice the anger without feeding it.
You don't have to fix everything today; just picture what leaving the gift and going might look like: a knock on a door, a call, I'm sorry for my part.
If it isn't safe to reach out, simply let the anger rest, and if you pray, you can bring that person with you into your prayer.
